items.title: Nintendo might be suing them, but Palworld CEO would still "love" to talk about bringing the survival game to Switch 2
items.summary: "We think the Switch 2 is a really amazing platform," says Pocketpair
items.content:
"We think the Switch 2 is a really amazing platform," says Pocketpair's Takuro Mizobe

(Image credit: Pocketpair) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Palworld developer Pocketpair may be in the midst of a legal battle with Nintendo and The Pokemon Company , but that's apparently not putting it off from the idea of bringing its hit survival game to Switch 2.

Pokemon and Nintendo filed a patent infringement lawsuit against Pocketpair over two years ago now, but even last year, prior to the Switch 2's launch, Pocketpair communications lead and publishing manager John "Bucky" Buckley said that porting Palworld to the platform was "100% worth considering" as long as the console was "beefy enough" to handle it.

And now, speaking in a new interview with VGC , Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe says "of course" he still sees this idea as a real possibility. "First of all, I should say that we think the Switch 2 is a really amazing platform, not just for games globally, but especially here in Japan and for the Japanese games industry," he begins.

"It's been an incredible platform. If there's ever a future where we have the opportunity to discuss or consider bringing Palworld to the Switch platform in some way, then we'd love to have those conversations."

He's clearly not just saying that, either. After all, Pocketpair launched another of its games, the roguelike tower defense and card game title Overdungeon, on Switch at the start of last year, so the lawsuit isn't making it avoid Nintendo's platforms entirely.

New Nintendo Switch 2 games for 2026 and beyond Pocketpair lead says "TemTem are not our rivals" as it gets its own Palworld-like survival game Pocketpair lead thought if Palworld 1.0 hit 200k players, "that'd be party time" – it passed 900k Of course, the situation may be a tad more complicated when it comes to the idea of porting the very game at the center of the ongoing lawsuit, but Pocketpair and its boss at the very least aren't personally opposed, despite the circumstances. Perhaps when the lawsuit has been resolved – one way or another – we could finally see Palworld on the platform. After all, it's certainly "beefy" enough to support the likes of Cyberpunk 2077, the Final Fantasy 7 Remake trilogy, and Elden Ring.

Palworld Side By Side is update 1.1 in a fancy hat, Pocketpair dev clarifies, not a new game or a "massive update."

items.title: Pocketpair CEO on keeping the indie spirit alive after Palworld’s success
items.summary: Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe says the studio won’t let Palworld’s success dictate what comes next…
items.content:
Interview Pocketpair CEO on keeping the indie spirit alive after Palworld’s success Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe says the studio won’t let Palworld’s success dictate what comes next

There’s an openness to Palworld developer Pocketpair that feels unusual in the games industry.

Its office in Gotanda, an up-and-coming entertainment district in Tokyo, is almost entirely open plan. From the CEO’s desk to the kitchen vending machines, there are no dividing walls, and the developer seems unconcerned with maintaining the air of secrecy that surrounds so many Japanese studios – even with a news journalist strolling around.

On social media, it has one of the most active community managers in the business, and visitors are often welcomed to drop by, stroll through its banks of developer desks, and have a go on the Palworld [111 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/palworld/ >Palworld -branded UFO catcher. It’s a far cry from other famous Japanese studios, which have been known to limit visits to closed meeting rooms and, sometimes, deny requests to use the bathroom.

Its approachability is particularly striking for a developer whose breakout success brought it a level of scrutiny that few independent studios experience. Palworld was barely out of the gate when its creature designs and eclectic combination of familiar mechanics attracted accusations of being derivative.

And then, of course, there was the Japanese lawsuit brought by The Pokémon Company , which alleges patent infringement, separate from the criticism that some of its creature designs bear conspicuous similarities to existing Pokémon video games [1,330 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/pokemon/ >Pokémon (with some later redesigned ).

At VGC, we extensively covered the controversy around Palworld in its early days and, more recently, published a 3/5 review of its 1.0 update . In my experience, other studios might have hunkered down, but it’s admirable that none of this changed Pocketpair’s willingness to talk.

Rather than dismissing our coverage, Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe [74 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/people/takuro-mizobe/ >Takuro Mizobe was keen to hear my take on why Palworld, a game that has clearly resonated hugely with players, so far has a critical consensus that doesn’t quite match the enthusiasm of players. The only off-limits topic was that Nintendo [6,912 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/platforms/nintendo/ >Nintendo lawsuit, which Pocketpair said they couldn’t legally comment on.

Mizobe attributes Pocketpair’s openness to its unusual origins. Founded in 2015, the company grew out of his experience in web and technology businesses, rather than the traditional Japanese games industry.

“When I think about it, perhaps the Japanese games industry is a little more closed,” he told VGC. “But I don’t think that’s because companies are trying to hide anything or because they don’t want to be transparent.

“Historically, Japanese companies have placed a lot of importance on protecting their employees, maintaining security, and protecting information. Without going too deeply into the history of Japanese business, there have been a lot of hard lessons learned over the years.

“But Pocketpair didn’t really start in that traditional way. We started as a group of friends coming from web culture, and we’ve always had a very open-source kind of culture. Very early on, we set up a Discord server for our players, and we’ve always had this very open style of communication with our community.”

That culture has survived a transformation few could have predicted when Mizobe formed the company in 2015 with fellow university students. Pocketpair’s first game, card-action title Overdungeon, established its formula of combining eclectic genres together. Its next game, the Zelda- and Minecraft [375 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/games/minecraft/ >Minecraft -inspired Craftopia, gave Pocketpair its first big hit, selling over one million copies.

But nothing could prepare it for the near-overnight success of Palworld’s early access version, which launched for Xbox [11,886 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/platforms/xbox/ >Xbox and PC [13,145 articles]" href=https://www.videogameschronicle.com/platforms/pc/ >PC in January 2024 and amassed 25 million players in a single month (it now has more than 40m, according to the studio).

items.title: Palworld's First Official Toy Collection Is Here, Complete With Mystery Eggs and Adorable Pals
items.summary: Collectibles creator The Loyal Subjects has released the game's first official toy collection, featuring everything from articulated figures to mystery eggs.
items.content:
It's a good time to be a Palworld obsessive. The game recently teased its next update, Palworld: Side by Side , coming this winter, and now collectibles creator The Loyal Subjects has released the game's first official toy collection, featuring everything from articulated figures to mystery eggs. It's available now on Amazon .

Decorate your desk with the frankly adorable Chillet, take everyone's favorite oversized electric menace Grizzbolt out and about, and keep the perpetually vacant-looking Relaxasaurus in your pocket to remind you not to scream at your boss.

There are four different products in the collection, starting with a range of 4-inch articulated figures featuring Foxparks, Relaxasaurus, Grizzbolt, and Lifmunk. Each comes with its own Battle FX accessory, so you can make them fight without having to worry about a raid on your base.

For those who prefer their Pals a little smaller, because it's not the size of the Pal that matters but what you do with it that counts, there's also a 3-inch collector set featuring Chillet, Grizzbolt, and Relaxasaurus ( see at Amazon ).

And because apparently collecting Pals in the game wasn't enough, there are two different mystery collections to hunt down. The Cheebee Micro Blind Mystery Pal Egg 12-Pack includes a dozen 1.5-inch mystery figures, while the Blind Egg Incubator Reveal 8-Pack offers eight miniature Pals to hatch and collect.

As always, the blind-box format means there's no guarantee you'll get the Pal you're after, so happy hunting to all the completionists out there. At least these ones won't require you to craft hundreds of Pal Spheres.

The collection is available to pre-order now on Amazon .

Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

items.title: Palworld Officially Teases the Game's Version 1.1 Update
items.summary: Palworld is formally giving fans an early teaser about the next major content update coming to the monster-catching survival game.
items.content:
Palworld Officially Teases the Game's Version 1.1 Update From GameRant (Written by Michael Brandon Ingram) on October 26, 2026 | OpenCritic

Palworld has dropped a brand-new teaser for the game's upcoming Version 1.1 patch, revealing the official title and release window for the next big update. Palworld officially launched its Version 1.0 and welcomed the game's full release in July 2026 after more than two years in early access.

The monster-catching survival game from developer Pocketpair was one of the biggest breakout hits in gaming following its debut. The game drew plenty of comparisons to the Pokemon franchise for its litany of unique creatures that fans can collect, combining monster-catching with survival and base-building elements. Palworld has added a wealth of content since the game's early access debut, significantly expanding the explorable area and even unveiling the mysterious World Tree with the Version 1.0 patch. Now, Pocketpair is getting fans excited about the next big update coming to the game.

Bushiroad is teasing a set of special promo cards coming to the Palworld Official Card Game as part of the game's newest release.

items.title: Pocketpair Talks Palworld – Expansions, Spinoffs and the Future
items.summary: Pocketpair talks about Palworld with MP1st, and discusss the game's future, DLC plans, spinoffs and a lot more.
items.content:
Possibly one of the biggest surprises of 2024 is Pocketpair’s Palworld . Originally thought of as just a Pokémon clone, the game has proven to be a lot more than that.

While most games lose steam after a year or two, Palworld shot back into the spotlight with the launch of its 1.0 state earlier this year.

With that in mind, we were able to talk to the studio about the hit game, their thoughts on expansions, and what to expect from update 1.1 and more.

Answering the questions is Pocketpair’s John “Bucky” Buckley, the studio’s Head of Publishing and Communications

MP1st : The release of Version 1.0 was met with tremendous success – so much so that the game’s player base started climbing back up again. Where else can Pocketpair take this?

Bucky : We’re so proud of how far Palworld has come, and version 1.0 being a success was a very special moment for us.

There are still many things we want to explore, both within the game itself and across the wider Palworld IP. At the same time, we don’t want to expand simply for the sake of making things bigger. Palworld is already a very large game, so we want to make sure if we do add new content to it then it will feel meaningful.

What matters most to us is continuing to create things that players find fun, surprising, and memorable. As long as we can keep doing that, we believe there is still a lot of room for Palworld to grow.

MP1st : Palworld doesn’t really follow the traditional live-service model of seasonal content drops. Is that something the studio is looking to do at some point? Or does the studio prefer larger, more premium (read: paid) content drops/DLC?

Bucky : We don’t think Palworld needs to follow a traditional live-service model simply because that approach works for other games. In the first place, we don’t even consider Palworld a “live service” game.

Rather than committing ourselves to a fixed seasonal cadence or a particular monetization model, we prefer to first think about what we want to create, and then choose the format that makes the most sense for that content.

Sometimes that may mean smaller updates, and sometimes it may mean something much larger. We want the content itself to determine the format, rather than the other way around.

MP1st : With Sony’s announcement that it plans to go all-digital in the future, has that affected Pocketpair’s output or what the studio plans to release on PlayStation platforms?

Bucky : From our perspective, our focus is simply on making Palworld available to as many players as we reasonably can, and providing the best experience on the platforms we support. We haven’t released any physical versions of our games up to now, so it’s a bit difficult for us to comment on the current state of physical distribution for games.

Alongside the occasional small patch, Palworld has just had its next big update announced for Winter 2026.

Officially dubbed the “Side by Side update,” the teaser image for it shows a few of the human Palworld Tower Bosses posing with weapons in their hands. Combine these two facts, and it seems to imply that this update will add the defeated bosses as potential companions for you to recruit as part of your adventure – a highly requested feature.

Source: Pocketpair Alongside this news come the results of the popularity poll that was released last month, finding out who the Palworld community likes the most. With two polls conducted, one for Pals and one for humans, the top picks for each have been revealed.

In the human category, the results are, frankly, predictable. Zoe came out on top yet again. As she is the first Tower Boss in the game, and currently the only one with a storyline following her defeat, it makes sense that she would be the character players have the deepest connection with.

Source: Pocketpair However, there may be more at play, as it’s worth pointing out that all five female characters took the top five spots, with the player character (who can be either gender) taking sixth, and everyone from seventh down being men. Do with that information what you will.

The Pal category was also unsurprising, as of all the new Pals added since the game first launched into early access, none have captured the community’s imagination like Sekhmet, the poll’s winner. Her cutesy catgirl aesthetic is an immediate draw, and combine that with the cute way she dances while idling around your base, and you have a sure-fire winner. Solenne took second place, while one of the game’s mascots, Chillet, took third.

and Stability Improvements ・Reduced load from some rendering processes, foliage display, and effect playback ・Reduced stuttering when some passive skills activate ・Reduced field rendering load in the World Tree area and other locations ▼Major Bug Fixes▼ ▼Crashes and Progression Issues ・Fixed an issue where controls could stop working after being returned to the title screen due to a connection before accepting the mission ・Fixed an issue where performing specific actions after ending dialogue with an NPC could prevent further dialogue ▼Pals and NPCs ・Fixed an issue where logging work would not occur for trees that respawned inside a base ・Fixed an issue where Visitors could spawn in unreachable locations ・Fixed an issue where dialogue would no longer occur if an NPC inside a base entered combat during dialogue ▼Partner Skills and Passive Skills ・Fixed an issue where Killamari Primo’s Partner Skill Lv. 2 and Lv. 3 effects were reversed ・Fixed an issue where Mutated Eggs increased by Grintale’s Passive Skill did not reflect mutated stat values ・Fixed an issue where the Idiosyncratic mutation passive did not activate correctly ・Fixed an issue where the defense bonus indicators could fail to appear during certain attacks in the World Tree boss battle ・Fixed an issue where removing a skill while it was being used could prevent that skill from being used afterward ・Fixed an issue where some attacks used by summoned Pals while other skills were on cooldown could also put unused skills on cooldown ・Fixed an issue that could occur when interrupting Ophydia’s after taking a certain amount of damage, or fail to summon smaller Pals correctly ・Fixed an issue where aiming while riding could make movement speed extremely slow ・Fixed an issue where wild Pals items.title: Now Available on TCGplayer: Palworld Official Card Game and Cyberpunk TCG
items.summary: We are excited to announce full support for all currently available products for Palworld Official Card Game and Cyberpunk TCG.
items.content:
Return to Seller Blog Post Tags #new TCG , #new product lines , #New Game , #bushiroad , #Palworld , #Cyberpunk TCG , #Palworld Official Card Game Now Available on TCGplayer: Palworld Official Card Game and Cyberpunk TCG By Jan Trovato • August 31, 2026 It’s a two-title launch: Palworld Official Card Game and Cyberpunk TCG are now available to list on the TCGplayer Marketplace!

The newest card game to debut from the publisher Bushiroad ( Cardfight Vanguard, Weiss Schwarz, etc.), Palworld Official Card Game reached explosive levels of popularity nearly overnight after its launch on July 30 of this year.

At the same time, Cyberpunk TCG is an up-and-coming card game slated to release November, but Kickstarter backers will be receiving some highly-anticipated, exclusive “preem” product in early September.

We are excited to announce full support for all currently available products for Palworld Official Card Game and Cyberpunk TCG. This includes sealed and singles for the first Palworld booster set, “Dawn of Palpagos” as well as the first two Trial Decks and any exclusive promotional cards. As for Cyberpunk TCG, all the products from the Kickstarter campaign (such as the booster box, the pre-built starter decks, and the Kickstarter exclusive cards) will also be available.

Sellers are now able to list their inventory for both Palworld Official Card Game and Cyberpunk TCG prior to the games’ launch on the TCGplayer Marketplace.

For more information on these card games, please visit the Palworld Official Card Game and Cyberpunk TCG official websites.

Have questions or feedback for our team? Contact us at catalog@tcgplayer.com .

items.title: v1.0.3: Balance Adjustments & Bug Fixes
items.summary: \ Palworld version v1.0.3 has been released! ＝＝＝ \ ▼Items and Equipment ・Changed the unlock level of some Jetragon-related technologies from 79 to 70, and reduced the materials required for the Pal Gear used to ride Jetragon. ・Changed the t
items.content:
\

Palworld version v1.0.3 has been released!

＝＝＝

\

▼Items and Equipment ・Changed the unlock level of some Jetragon-related technologies from 79 to 70, and reduced the materials required for the Pal Gear used to ride Jetragon.

・Changed the technology unlock level of the Aquatic Construction Kit from Level 66 to Level 23, changed its Ancient Technology Point requirement from 4 to 1, and adjusted the required materials and work amount.

・Extended the duration of World Tree Holy Water.

・Reduced the weight of World Tree Holy Water from 1 to 0.1.

・Added World Tree Holy Water to the rewards for World Tree expeditions, World Tree fishing, and the Large Fishing Pond.

・Increased the amount of World Tree Holy Water obtained from Pals in The World Tree area.

・Increased the amount of World Tree Holy Water obtained from Teafant Spring.

・Adjusted the work amount required to craft the Ancient Armor series.

・Doubled the amount of Fiber obtained from trees.

▼Bases and Missions

・Reduced the building costs of the Crude Oil Extractor, High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor, and Large Power Generator.

・Increased the crude oil production speed of the Crude Oil Extractor and High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor.

・The base mission that requires building a Crude Oil Extractor can now also be progressed by building a High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor.

▼Server Settings

・Added a server setting (bAllowEnemyCampSpawnNearBaseCamp) that disables the suppression of enemy camp spawns near player base camps.

\

▼Graphics and Display

・Adjusted the boundary display in some areas to make it easier to see from a distance.

・Improved the display quality of some objects in dungeons.

▼Sound

・Added a sound effect when using World Tree Holy Water.

\

▼Crashes and Progression Blockers

・Fixed an issue where the mission could become impossible to progress if the barrier was removed before accepting the main mission in Sunreach.

▼Multiplayer and Co-op

・Fixed an issue in co-op where lighting on the client side could display incorrectly after cutscenes or the ending played.

・Fixed an issue in co-op where some scenes could stutter during the cutscene that plays when entering The World Tree.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where Fast Travel could activate unintentionally during Tower Boss battles.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where Pals could appear to vibrate rapidly on the client screen.

▼Pals and NPCs

・Fixed an issue where the summoned Pal could stop fighting.

・Fixed an issue where the summoned Pal could stop helping with base work.

・Fixed an issue in multiplayer where, when the Partner Skill of Orserk or certain other Pals activated, the effect display could fail to update correctly, making it appear as though the skill had not activated.

・Fixed an issue where Alpha Surfent would not produce Leather when assigned to a Ranch.

▼Battles and Bosses

・Fixed an issue where some raid boss battles could fail to progress as intended.

・Fixed an issue where the wave effect and actual damage range did not match for some of Panthalus's attacks.

▼Bases and Building

・Fixed an issue where the placement detection for stairs and slanted roofs could fail to match their actual shape.

・Fixed an issue where stairs could not be placed correctly on the sides of foundations or roofs.

▼Items and Rewards

・Fixed an issue where the reward settings for the normal Moon Lord battle and the Ultra Raid Boss battle had not been updated to the intended settings.

・Fixed an issue where items could duplicate when performing certain actions.

・Fixed an issue where, when Katress's Partner Skill activated, switching spheres while riding could allow the player to obtain a different type of sphere.

・Fixed an issue where the World Tree Holy Water effect did not display correctly on the Pal being ridden when using World Tree Holy Water while riding.

・Fixed an issue where, after the World Tree Holy Water effect ended, riding a Pal would cause the World Tree Holy Water aura to reappear and not disappear when approaching trees in The World Tree area.

・Fixed an issue where an unintended reward was set for the desert expedition.

・Fixed an issue where the Dark Skill Fruit: Psycho Gravity did not appear on the item search screen.

・Fixed a bug where the firing interval was not set for sphere launchers

▼UI, Display, and Text

・Fixed an issue where resolution settings would not apply correctly in fullscreen mode.

・Fixed an issue where, after switching window mode with F11 / Alt+Enter, the game could unintentionally return to fullscreen mode after loading.

・Fixed an issue where, if certain effects were on screen while aiming, the entire screen could become blurred.

▼Sound

・Fixed an issue where the water sound effect could fail to play at Teafant Spring.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where the BGM for Attack Choppers triggered by other players could play even from far away.

・Adjusted the BGM playback range for Attack Choppers so that it plays correctly for players who are Wanted.

・Fixed an issue where unintended footstep sounds could play when walking on furniture or facilities.

▼Controls

・Fixed an issue where, after changing the key assignment for ""Attack that enemy!"" in Controls, selecting ""Restore to Default"" would not restore the default setting.

・Fixed an issue where settings could be applied unintentionally when interacting with the change confirmation dialog and duplicate key warning in Controls.

▼Map and Exploration

・Fixed an issue where a beach-like display could remain on the water surface after Fast Traveling to an offshore base.

＝＝＝

Thank you for your continued support of Palworld.
